The correct symmetric reduction is  
\[
\frac{3(a^3-6)\sqrt[3]{a+6}}{3a^2}=\frac{(a^3-6)\sqrt[3]{a+6}}{a^2}.
\]
At \(a=2\), this gives \(1\).

To prove this is maximal, set
\[
g(t)=(t^3-6)\sqrt[3]{t+6}.
\]
If \(t^3\le 6\), then \(g(t)\le 0<t^2\).  
If \(\sqrt[3]{6}<t\le2\), then
\[
h(t)=\frac{g(t)}{t^2}
\]
satisfies
\[
\frac{h'(t)}{h(t)}
=\frac{3t^2}{t^3-6}+\frac{1}{3(t+6)}-\frac2t
> \frac{3t^2}{2}-\frac2t
=\frac{3t^3-4}{2t}>0.
\]
So \(h(t)\le h(2)=1\), hence \(g(t)\le t^2\) for all \(t\in(0,2]\).

Thus
\[
A\le \frac{x^2+y^2+z^2}{x^2+y^2+z^2}=1.
\]
Equality occurs at \(x=y=z=2\).

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
